children: CME livestock futures are mixed in morning trading, ahead of the USDA's monthly WASDE report, due out at noon Eastern time. Livestock has been generally weak in recent trade, typical for the time after the Labor Day holiday, says ADM Investor Services in a note. "Consumers spend less during September after the expenditures of summer, school expenses and saving for the end of the year holidays and now with higher energy cost more consumers are having to spend less," says the firm. Live cattle futures are up 0.8%, while lean hogs are down 0.7%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
